messages:
maria_support: Hey team — customer report: multiple EU customers from different ISPs seeing our hosted API route to us-west and getting intermittent 401s + big retry spikes on billing. They saw it start ~10:15 UTC. Any quick checks?

samir_oncall: Ugh, saw alerts for increased token usage and 401 rate from that customer org. I can repro from my laptop (eu VM) — curl to api.redwood.ai returns 401 and headers show x-edge: us-west-2.

ingrid_prod: That sounds like GeoIP misroute. Can you paste the dig + trace? Also which resolver they use?

samir_oncall: Repro steps I ran:
```
dig +short api.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8
;; -> returns 13.32.14.7 (us-west)
```
then
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (13.32.14.7) port 443
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
```
Token is valid in other regions.

jay_devops: Can you also run `dig +trace api.redwood.ai` and `dig NS api.redwood.ai`? I want to see if delegation changed.

samir_oncall: dig +trace shows the authoritative NS set with different zone serials across a subset of authoritative servers. `dig @ns1.example-dns  SOA api.redwood.ai` returns serial 20240315.1 but `@ns3.example-dns` returns 20240228.2.

maria_support: That would explain some resolvers hitting stale NS and getting older geodb data, right?

ingrid_prod: Yes — if an authoritative server still has the old zone it can return A records that point to the wrong edge. Our edge selection relies on a GeoIP table that was updated 2024-03-15 to add new EU PoPs. If resolver goes to old NS, it could answer with legacy IPs that map to us-west.

tariq_netops: Possible causes: partial zone push failure, propagation stuck on a subset of NS, or some upstream mirror not syncing. I'll check the DNS provider's push logs.

dns-bot: automated: noticed a failed AXFR to ns3.example-dns at 2024-11-17T10:12:03Z — retry queued.

jay_devops: Ok that's consistent. Mitigation plan: 1) Force zone re-push to all authoritative nameservers, 2) lower TTL for the critical record to 60s for next rollout, 3) add short-term fallback policy to prefer eu-* pool when region header absent.

ingrid_prod: For customer-facing mitigation we should also instruct them to flush their resolver cache or switch to a different resolver (e.g., 1.1.1.1) while we fix authoritative sync. But we can't ask every customer. Suggest we roll a config: if incoming IP maps to unexpected region AND auth token indicates eu tenant, return 302 to eu endpoint or validate token region headers earlier to reduce 401s.

maria_support: Can we reduce billing spike? Retries come from clients hitting 401 then retry loops — maybe return 429 with Retry-After instead of 401 when region mismatch suspected?

samir_oncall: We can add a short-circuit: if auth check fails but IP is non-local and token issuer is EU, respond with 409 + header `X-Region-Mismatch: eu` so SDK can short-circuit retries. Quick patch workable?

ingrid_prod: Yes, small gateway change. I'll open a canary PR and route to eu-only test tenants first. Also tagging SRE to monitor errors.

tariq_netops: Pushed zone repush and forced AXFR. Providers show successful sync to ns3 at 10:29 UTC. I also bumped A-record TTL down to 60 for the next 10m window.

dns-bot: automated: AXFR to ns3.example-dns succeeded at 2024-11-17T10:29:12Z.

samir_oncall: Re-tested from eu VM: `dig @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.ai` -> now returns eu edge IPs. curl with same token returns 200. No more 401s.

maria_support: Took note in support ticket and told customer: "We've applied a fix to DNS propagation and applied a temporary gateway rule to reduce retries. Please retry now and let us know if you still see issues."

jay_devops: Follow-ups: 1) Add health-check on NS serial parity (alert if serials diverge by >1), 2) Add automated roll-forward for partial AXFR failures, 3) Review push pipeline to avoid partial pushes. I'll create backlog tickets.

ingrid_prod: Also schedule a postmortem with DNS provider to find root cause. Short-term post-incident action: add `X-Region-Mismatch` guidance to SDKs so clients implement friendly retry behavior.

maria_support: Thanks all. I'll close the ticket once customer confirms. :thumbsup:
